clinician.trajectory_summary: A 63-year-old man presented with left lower extremity swelling and pain for one week and was empirically treated with rivaroxaban by his PCP. Lower extremity Doppler ultrasound confirmed extensive occlusive deep vein thrombosis involving the left calf, femoral, and superficial veins, as well as chronic occlusive DVT in the right popliteal veins. A venogram was performed that confirmed the diagnosis of May-Thurner Syndrome with iliac vein compression, patent distal inferior vena cava, and the catheter tip positioned within the IVC, consistent with the diagnosis of MTS.

Venogram confirmed iliac vein compression diagnostic of May-Thurner Syndrome with patent distal IVC and catheter tip in the IVC.
